subject: E2E latency banding & streaming constraints — Acme POC next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: E2E latency banding & streaming constraints — Acme POC next steps

Olivia / Acme SRE team — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist for the POC.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: verify your live workload meets the product SLAs when switched to Redwood hosted inference. You emphasized user-facing latency and streaming fidelity.
- Current provider metrics (as discussed): p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms (measured at your app edge).
- Payload profile: median request ~220 tokens, 95th payload size ~780 tokens; streaming expected for interactive UX.
- Concurrency needs: bursts to 200 concurrent streaming sessions; steady-state throughput target ~600–800 rps for the POC.

Key open questions we need from you (please confirm in reply):
1) End-to-end measurement point: do you want Redwood to measure from our edge to return (server-side), or will you measure client-side from the browser/app? We recommend primary acceptance be client-side p95/p99 to reflect user experience, but we can provide server-side metrics for debugging.
2) Payload mix: can you share a simple CSV with the token-size distribution and a few sample payloads (attachments OK) so we can mirror the profile?
3) Streaming contract: do you need single-chunk latency guarantees or sustained chunk delivery (e.g., first-byte p95 and full-response p95/p99)?
4) Failure/fallback behavior: what is acceptable—degraded streaming (lower quality) or failover to current vendor?

Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Client-side E2E p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 550ms for interactive requests where payload <= 512 tokens.
- For payloads between 512–1024 tokens expect p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 900ms (we'll measure separately).
- Sustained streaming concurrency: support 200 concurrent char-by-char streams with end-to-end p95/p99 within above bands across a 15-minute window.
- Throughput: 800 rps sustained for 5 minutes with <1% error budget.

Suggested next steps
- Olivia: share the token distribution CSV and confirm whether acceptance will be client-side (preferred).
- Redwood (Marcus + Ben): produce a test plan + short-hosted vs current provider summary and run a controlled benchmark (we'll attach the summary pdf).
- Schedule engineering sync for a live run next week (we suggested Wed 2027-04-21, 10:00 PDT).

Attachments: acme-latency-profile.csv (placeholder) — please attach the CSV you mentioned on the call. We'll attach a short Redwood-hosted-vs-current-summary.pdf after internal prep.

Thanks — will turn this into a HubSpot task after your reply.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items and answering your Qs below.

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 3:10 PM Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> Olivia / Acme SRE team — thanks again for the call today. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist for the POC.
> ...

Answers / clarifications:
- Measurement point: primary acceptance will be client-side (we measure from the browser edge, so client-side p95/p99 is the source of truth). We can provide server-side traces but the acceptance thresholds should be measured client-side.
- Token distribution CSV: attached (acme-latency-profile.csv) — includes 10k sampled requests and token counts. The csv column headers: timestamp, request_id, tokens, latency_ms_current_provider_edge.
- Streaming: we require both first-byte and sustained chunk rates. For interactive flows, first-byte matters for perceived latency (first-byte p95 target ~200–300ms). We also expect chunks to continue at a minimum cadence such that total time-to-first-meaningful-update meets the p95 bands above.
- Fallbacks: acceptable to failover to current provider if Redwood returns >5% errors during the test window. We want a canary with automatic fallback.

Numbers from our monitoring (production current provider, measured at app edge): p95 180ms, p99 420ms for the interactive route. We will target up to 200 concurrent streams during the POC.

We can do the test window Wed 2027-04-21 10:00 PDT. Please provide the Redwood test harness and the specific endpoint to hit so our SREs can coordinate.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product Operations, Acme AI
olivia@acme.ai
+1 (646) 888-1993

Olivia — perfect, thanks for the CSV and the confirmation on client-side measurement. Below is a short, concrete test plan and acceptance checklist we'll execute for Wed 2027-04-21 10:00 PDT.

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 9:35 AM Olivia Park <olivia@acme.ai> wrote:
> Marcus — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming items and answering your Qs below.
> ...

Redwood POC test plan (high level)
1) Pre-run: Redwood runs a mirrored baseline against your current provider using the attached token distribution to validate our synthetic harness matches observed shapes.
2) Measurement points:
   - Client-side synthetic runner inside Acme infra (your runner will call our hosted endpoint). We will instrument and report both client-side and server-side (for debugging).
   - We'll capture first-byte, last-byte, chunk cadence, and total time-to-first-meaningful-update.
3) Load profile:
   - Ramp to 800 rps steady for 5 minutes, with 200 concurrent streaming clients during peak.
   - Run three 15-minute windows to gather sample variance.
4) Acceptance thresholds (proposed final):
   - Client-side E2E: p95 <= 250ms (<=512 tokens), p99 <= 550ms (<=512 tokens).
   - First-byte p95 <= 300ms for interactive payloads.
   - Error rate < 1% and fallback behavior triggers if >5% errors in 15 minute window.
5) Reporting: Redwood will provide a short report with p50/p90/p95/p99 curves (CSV + one-page PDF) and request traces for any outliers.

Action items for Wed run
- Redwood: provide test endpoint, auth token, and the harness runner (we'll supply a GH gist with the harness scripts).
- Acme: validate client-side runner and coordinate SRE for timing.
- Both: agree on a 1-hour window after the run to triage results.

We'll attach a short summary PDF (redwood-hosted-vs-current-summary.pdf) with our baseline numbers by EOD today. Marcus — Ben and I will join the run; I'll loop in the infra team.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
